description_good_justification: README.md opens with a one-line description ('C2PA Manifest Store embedding and reading for ZIP-based (OCF-style) documents: EPUB, DOCX, ODT, OXPS') and an Overview section explaining the ZIP embedding transport.
interact_justification: README.md documents install (`cargo add`, `npm install`, `pip install`), CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to file issues and submit PRs, and the repo is public at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip for feedback via Issues.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section: fork, branch from main, add tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies coding/acceptance requirements: cargo test --all-features, cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, and Conventional Commits style.
floss_license_justification: Dual-licensed under Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-APACHE) and MIT (LICENSE-MIT); Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0".
floss_license_osi_justification: Both Apache License 2.0 and the MIT License are OSI-approved licenses (https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0, https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT); text in LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT matches the standard license text.
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents installation, Quick Start usage (embed/read/remove/verify), and Design/Scope sections; src/lib.rs carries //! crate-level rustdoc.
documentation_interface_justification: Public API (embed_manifest, read_manifest, remove_manifest, verify, collection_members, central_directory_range) is documented via rustdoc in src/lib.rs and published at https://docs.rs/c2pa-zip (linked from README.md badge); #![warn(missing_docs)] in src/lib.rs enforces doc coverage on public items.
sites_https_justification: Repo is hosted at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip (HTTPS); all README/CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/CODE_OF_CONDUCT links observed use https:// (crates.io, docs.rs, github.com, c2pa.org, w3.org, iso.org, ecma-international.org); no http:// links found in these files.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled and used (e.g. https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/issues, with templates at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml), is URL-addressable, publicly searchable, and open to any GitHub user without a proprietary client.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) is written in English; issue templates are in English.
maintained_justification: git log shows active commits through 2026-08-24/2026-08-25 (e.g. commit 318146e '318146e docs: add title...' and 9b3d71d 'ci(security): pin actions by SHA' dated Aug 2026), with two releases (v0.1.0 on 2026-07-31, v0.2.0 on 2026-08-02) and ongoing dependabot PR merges within the last week.
repo_public_justification: Public GitHub repo at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip (confirmed via `gh repo view`: isPrivate=false), using git.
repo_track_justification: git is used; `git log` shows author, timestamp, and message for every commit (e.g. 'David Condrey <davidcondrey@me.com>').
repo_interim_justification: git log between v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 tags shows many interim commits (e.g. 78d3037, 352ee55, 8779c12, b12da8c, f2c5ad7, 526e91b) beyond just the two release commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml version = "0.2.0" and git tags v0.1.0, v0.2.0 give each release a unique SemVer identifier; release.yml enforces that the pushed tag matches Cargo.toml's version before publishing.
version_semver_justification: Versions follow SemVer (0.1.0, 0.2.0 per `git tag` and Cargo.toml version field).
version_tags_justification: `git tag` lists v0.1.0 and v0.2.0, matching GitHub Releases at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/releases/tag/v0.2.0 and .../v0.1.0.
release_notes_justification: GitHub Releases for v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 (via `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/releases`) contain only an auto-generated 'What's Changed'/'Full Changelog' compare link, not curated human-readable release notes; no CHANGELOG.md exists in the repo root despite cliff.toml being present for git-cliff changelog generation, and it is not being used to produce one yet.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in this project's history (no CVEs, no vulnerability-labeled commits found in `git log`), so there are no vulnerability fixes that would need identification in release notes.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues with templates at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml, feature_request.yml, and config.yml provide a public bug-report process.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/issues) is used as the per-issue tracker, evidenced by numbered issues/PRs #1-#16 from `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/issues`.
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: All issues observed in the last 2-12 months (via `gh api .../issues` and `.../issues?state=closed`) are automated dependabot dependency-update PRs (#1-#16), which were promptly reviewed and merged (e.g. #12-#15 merged within days of creation, per closed_at vs created_at timestamps); no organic user bug report has been filed yet to demonstrate a non-automated response, but nothing has gone unacknowledged.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met — flag for maintainer confirmation if/when real reports arrive.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: No enhancement/feature requests have been filed yet (issue history via `gh api` is entirely dependabot PRs #1-#16), so there is no backlog of unaddressed requests; vacuously satisfied pending real requests.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/issues (both open and closed) is publicly viewable and searchable without special access.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: private GitHub Security Advisory (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/security/advisories/new) or email admin@writerslogic.com, with guidance on what to include.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explicitly offers two private channels: GitHub Security Advisories (private by design) and direct email to admin@writerslogic.com, explicitly telling reporters not to use public issues.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (no security advisories or vulnerability-related issues found in repo history), so there is no response-time track record to evaluate.
build_justification: Rust crate built with `cargo build`/`cargo check` (see .github/workflows/ci.yml 'Check' job) plus wasm32 and Python (maturin/PyO3, pyproject.toml) build targets; CONTRIBUTING.md documents `cargo build`.
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, plus maturin for the Python wheel (pyproject.toml) and wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack conventions for the npm target — all standard tools for their respective ecosystems.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, maturin, and wasm-bindgen are all FLOSS; no proprietary build tool is required (verified via Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, and .github/workflows/ci.yml).
test_justification: tests/roundtrip.rs (175 lines, 8 #[test] functions) plus unit tests embedded in src/zip.rs (11), src/writer.rs (7), src/binding.rs (6), src/reader.rs (3), src/verify.rs (5), src/error.rs (2); documented to run via `cargo test` in README.md is implicit and explicit in CONTRIBUTING.md ('cargo test --all-features') and .github/workflows/ci.yml.
test_invocation_justification: Tests are run with the standard Rust invocation `cargo test` (and `cargo test --all-features`), documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and used in .github/workflows/ci.yml 'Test' job.
test_most_justification: 42 total #[test] functions across tests/roundtrip.rs and unit tests in src/zip.rs, writer.rs, binding.rs, reader.rs, verify.rs, error.rs cover embed/read/remove/verify round-trips, ZIP64 rejection, and error paths per README.md's Design section claims ('bounds-checked against untrusted input').
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo test --all-features` on every push/PR to main via GitHub Actions.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2 explicitly states: 'Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features'.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature commits added corresponding tests, e.g. commit 526e91b 'feat: uniform Error::code, verified MSRV, and integration tests' and 352ee55 'feat: add Python bindings and release workflow' followed by growth of tests/roundtrip.rs and per-module unit tests.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly documents the policy ('Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features') in the contribution instructions.
warnings_justification: .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml run `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; src/lib.rs also sets #![warn(missing_docs)].
warnings_fixed_justification: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) fails the build on any clippy warning (`-D warnings`), so warnings cannot merge unaddressed; commit e9cb2a2 'chore: harden lints, docs, and CI' shows active warning cleanup.
warnings_strict_justification: clippy is run with `-D warnings` (deny, not just warn) across --all-features --all-targets in CI, plus separate clippy runs for the wasm32 target and the python feature in release.yml, which is close to maximally strict for a Rust project; no clippy.toml restricting lint scope was found.
know_secure_design_justification: README.md's Design section documents deliberate security-relevant design choices (fail-closed rejection of ZIP64 archives, bounds-checked parsing of untrusted input, byte-offset preservation to avoid corrupting other entries) and src/lib.rs sets #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; SECURITY.md documents a supply-chain security posture (SHA-pinned Actions, Scorecard, Dependency Review, Dependabot, build provenance).
know_common_errors_justification: README.md and src/lib.rs explicitly call out untrusted-input handling for a ZIP parser (bounds-checking, ZIP64 fail-closed rejection to avoid mis-parsing) which is the class of error (buffer/offset handling on attacker-controlled archives) relevant to this software; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in src/lib.rs eliminates memory-safety errors by construction.
crypto_published_justification: Crate is a ZIP transport/parser only (per README.md 'Scope' section); it does not implement or select cryptographic algorithms — manifest signing is explicitly out of scope and delegated to the separate `c2pa` SDK.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate (README.md: 'Manifest construction, signing, and hard/soft binding ... are out of scope; use the c2pa SDK for those').
crypto_floss_justification: No cryptography is implemented in this crate.
crypto_keylength_justification: No cryptographic keys are generated or used by this crate.
crypto_working_justification: No cryptographic algorithms are implemented or selected by this crate.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptographic algorithms are implemented or selected by this crate.
crypto_pfs_justification: No key-agreement protocol is implemented; the crate has no network/transport layer.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The crate stores no passwords; it has no authentication functionality.
crypto_random_justification: The crate generates no cryptographic keys or nonces (Cargo.toml has zero non-optional dependencies and no RNG dependency).
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed via crates.io, npm, and PyPI, all served over HTTPS; source is cloned via https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip.git or git@github.com (SSH).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No separate unsigned hash-only integrity check is distributed over plain HTTP; packages are retrieved over HTTPS from crates.io/npm/PyPI, which serve package integrity metadata (checksums) over TLS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known public unpatched medium+ severity vulnerability exists for this project; commit 460fd34 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29' shows dependency vulnerabilities are addressed promptly, and Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) runs weekly.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported against this project to date; the SHA-pinning hardening commit (9b3d71d) and prompt pyo3 security bump (460fd34) demonstrate the project responds quickly when a security-relevant fix is needed.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Searched full `git log -p --all` for common credential patterns (api_key, secret, password, token assignments with long values); none found. Release workflow uses repository secrets (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN) and PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC), not embedded credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml).
static_analysis_justification: `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` (a FLOSS static analysis tool for Rust) runs on every CI build (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and again before every release (.github/workflows/release.yml).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: clippy's default lint set includes correctness and suspicious-pattern lints (e.g. arithmetic overflow, indexing, unwrap-on-Result) relevant to a parser handling untrusted byte input; combined with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in src/lib.rs this covers the main vulnerability classes for this crate (memory safety, integer/bounds errors).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI enforces `-D warnings` on clippy, so any medium+ finding blocks merge (.github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml); commit e9cb2a2 'chore: harden lints, docs, and CI' shows findings being actively addressed.
static_analysis_often_justification: clippy runs on every push and pull_request to main via .github/workflows/ci.yml, i.e. on every commit.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A cargo-fuzz target (fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_untrusted.rs) drives the crate's untrusted-input parsers with libFuzzer; fuzz/README.md documents how to run it.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No memory-unsafe code is present: src/lib.rs sets #![forbid(unsafe_code)], and the crate has zero non-optional dependencies (no C/C++ present via FFI in the core library; pyo3/wasm-bindgen bindings are optional feature-gated glue, not project-authored unsafe code).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz target builds with cargo-fuzz's default dev profile, which enables debug assertions and overflow checks, so Rust's integer-overflow and bounds checks act as assertions during fuzzing.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is currently run against this project, so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
